claude.sample_unit: simulated triage queries (single fixed symptom vignette with varied SES signals)

links.outcome: ER referral rate changes when only patient SES signal varied in prompts
links.effect: All three models raised ER referral for lower-SES patients given explicit signal (spreads 13-50 points); Gemini shifted 11.4 points pooled from ZIP code alone (p=1.4e-7); Claude -0.1; GPT-5.4-mini 2.0.
links.quote: All three models raise their emergency-room (ER) referral rate for lower-SES patients given the explicit signal (spreads of 13-50 percentage points).

unlisted_practices: Single-sentence system-prompt instruction to reduce SES-driven triage differences (reduced Gemini gap from 11.4 to 5.8 points)
Reasoning-trace audit is insufficient to detect demographic-driven output shifts

links.effect: Gemini ZIP effect 11.4 points (p = 1.4e-7; 6/6 pairs); Claude -0.1; GPT-5.4-mini 2.0 points, predicted direction 2/6.
links.quote: Critically, sensitivity to the implicit ZIP-code signal is model-dependent: Gemini infers SES from geography alone, shifting its ER rate by a pooled 11.4 points across six US ZIP-code pairs (p = 1.4e-7, same direction in 6/6 pairs), while Claude Sonnet 4.6 stays flat (-0.1 points) and GPT-5.4-mini shows only a small difference that is not sign-consistent (2.0 points, predicted direction in just 2 of 6 pairs), neither a reliable ZIP-code effect, despite both responding to the explicit signal.

links.outcome: system-prompt mitigation of ZIP SES gap
links.effect: Gemini gap between low- and high-income ZIPs fell from 11.4 to 5.8 points, reduced but not eliminated.
links.quote: A single-sentence system-prompt instruction reduces but does not eliminate the effect (Gemini's gap between low- and high-income ZIPs falls from 11.4 to 5.8 points).

unlisted_practices: Reasoning-trace audits for detecting socioeconomic triage shifts
